title: auth-api-401-429-debug-scratchpad-jamie-2026-03-04
body:
Goal: collect breadcrumbs and quick reproduction steps for recurring 401/429 patterns hitting Hosted API (primarily /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings).

Summary of incidents seen:
- 2026-03-02 09:18-09:24 UTC: burst of 429s for org=acme-corp, looks correlated with spike in embed jobs from ingest worker.
- 2026-03-03 14:05-14:12 UTC: intermittent 401s for several clients, same time as key rotation window on auth-service.
- 2026-03-04 02:30 UTC: single-tenant customer saw sustained 429s (~60s) even though dashboard shows remaining quota > 0.

Commands/traces I ran (local repro):
- Basic curl (valid token) -> 200:
  curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $GOOD_TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","input":"hello"}'

- With revoked token -> 401 snippet:
  HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
  Content-Type: application/json
  Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 14:07:01 GMT
  {"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key revoked"}

- Observed 429 with headers:
  HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
  X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
  X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
  Retry-After: 8
  {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"token rate limit exceeded"}

- Edge case: 401 but body is generic and audit log shows token still active in auth-db: (truncated)
  gateway.log: [2026-03-03T14:05:07Z] req_id=abc123 auth-check=cache-miss token_id=tok-9a8b => upstream auth-service returned 200 introspect=true
  gateway.log: [2026-03-03T14:05:07Z] req_id=abc123 auth-cache-set ttl=30s
  gateway.log: [2026-03-03T14:05:07Z] req_id=abc123 response=401 downstream

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Token rotation propagation gap: auth-service rotates or revokes keys, edge caches still have stale state leading to 401s or false positives for 401s when rotation is partial. Cache TTLs are 30s in gateway config (see gateway-config v2).
2) Burst-based quota enforcement: per-token or per-org rate limiter miscounts tokens after batching/aggregation (we recently changed batching in serving-runtime that aggregates small requests). Could under-count or double-count. Explains 429s when dashboard shows tokens left because dashboard queries a different counter (per-customer-month vs per-second sliding window).
3) Misapplied policy: Some routes (embeddings) are subject to a different quota key (route+model) and the rate-limit headers returned are for route-level not token-level, confusing clients.
4) Retry-After rounding: Retry-After small values cause client retries that pile and trigger subsequent 429s.
5) Auth introspection race: gateway caches an introspection result flagged as active but downstream model router rejects due to model-specific access control (missing model entitlement) causing 401-like failure.

Quick checks to run next: (prioritized)
- Reproduce a 401 with extra logging: set DEBUG_AUTH=1 on gateway to capture full introspection payload and which layer returned 401.
- Correlate gateway logs with auth-service audit: run query for token_id pattern and timestamps for 2026-03-03 14:00-14:10 UTC (ELK: index=auth-*, query=req_id OR token_id).
- Check cache TTLs on all gateway instances (zone edge vs central) — possible misaligned config after canary.
- Reproduce embed burst: run 100 parallel embed requests using a known test key and watch X-RateLimit-* headers and internal counters (metrics: rate_limiter.*).
- Confirm dashboard counters (billing service) vs runtime counters (limiter service) for the affected org; file JIRA if mismatch.

Known artifacts/notes:
- gateway-config v2 introduced in PR #402 (github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/402) changed introspection cache ttl from 60s -> 30s during canary (timeline matches 2026-03-03).
- rate-limiter service uses token bucket with shard key = org_id unless route-specific flag set. Last deploy 2026-02-28.
- Customer embed worker spikes are from pipeline job 'ingest-batch-runner' (k8s namespace batch-jobs).

Quick TODOs (assign & dates):
- [Jamie] Add extra debug header on next gateway deploy (DEBUG_AUTH=1) and enable for canary only - target 2026-03-05.
- [Lena] Pull auth audit logs for 2026-03-03 13:55-14:20 UTC and attach to JIRA-5821 - target 2026-03-04.
- [Oliver] Run synthetic embed-burst test (100 parallel) against staging limiter and capture metrics - target 2026-03-04.
- [All] Confirm whether billing counters differ from runtime counters - checklist below.

Checklist to validate counter mismatch:
- Confirm limiter metric rate_limiter.allowed_count and billing metric billing.requests_recorded for same time window.
- Check if billing pipeline filters out internal health checks that limiter counts.
- Verify shard key logic in limiter (org_id vs token_id) and if grouping was changed in last deploy.

Notes-to-self / small snippets:
- If we see X-RateLimit-Remaining negative -> likely race in atomic decrement (sharded redis Lua scripts).
- If 401s cluster around auth rotation window -> add distributed lock during revocation to avoid partial state.
- Watch for client-side caching of 401 responses (chrome-based SDKs sometimes cache 401 -> re-use)

Slack refs: see thread #api-errors-401-429: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02ABCD1234/p1616161616000
JIRA: JIRA-5821 (parent) -> currently labeled "investigate-401-429-patterns"
GitHub PRs: gateway PR #402, rate-limiter PR #377

If I get time: add simple repro harness (python) that hits both /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings with configurable concurrency and token rotation simulation. Save under /devtools/simulated-burst/ and share with Oliver.

End of scratchpad.
